issues.reason: Coordination & plurals states that a distributive predicate "also hands the predication to the group's members via a rule", and Quantifiers names a "grouped / counted plural" ("the dogs barked") as taking the per-member (PartOf $x <group>) rule beside the group event, so the nightmoth group's landing and leaving each owe a rule the parse never emits.

new_gaps: A plural-headed multi-word proper name ("the Salt-bloom Tide-pools"): Names and casing licenses one singular type atom for a kind word inside a name (Kestrel River -> river) and bars GroupOf / per-member kind on a plural name-label ("the Wrens"), so nothing licenses recording that the named referent is a SET of tide-pools - (Member salt_bloom_tide_pools tide_pool) is the only form on offer and it types a plurality as one pool.
defect_summary: Compliant form: beside each nightmoth group event, the per-member distribution rule over the group - (: nm_land (Implication (PartOf $x sk_nightmoth_1) (And (Member (sk_land $x) land) (Agent (sk_land $x) $x) (Location (sk_land $x) sk_lantern_1) (Time (sk_land $x) night) (Past (sk_land $x)))) (STV 1.0 0.9)) and the parallel (sk_leave $x) rule carrying (Theme ... sk_thread_1) and (Location ... sk_lantern_1); the group events and Before atoms stay as they are.
notes: The rest of the passage holds up against the instruction set: the silken_thread / nightmoth / sea_water / tide_pool / clay_vessel decompositions obey the noun-modifier bar, "by evening" is correctly TimeAtMost on a day-part, entity-attached From carries the sea-water's origin, and both past perfects get their Before against an asserted event. The reviewer was right to leave the sk_thread_1 reuse unfiled - the threads in sentence 3 are the ones already introduced, and Coreference licenses symbol reuse for a later mention of an introduced referent.
